::: {.patient-banner}
## Complex Dysphagia Evaluation

Today's simulation focuses on the evaluation of a medically complex patient with a tracheostomy and suspected oropharyngeal dysphagia. Students will integrate chart review, Passy-Muir Valve (PMV) assessment, bedside swallowing evaluation, interdisciplinary information, and clinical reasoning to develop appropriate recommendations.
:::

::: {.warning}
## SLP Task

Work through each module with your group. Review the patient's medical history and interdisciplinary documentation, determine readiness for PMV evaluation, complete a PMV and clinical swallowing evaluation, and develop recommendations regarding communication, oral intake, and need for further assessment.
:::

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this session, students will be able to:

- Integrate medical and interdisciplinary information relevant to PMV and swallowing evaluation.
- Determine readiness for Passy-Muir Valve assessment in a medically complex patient.
- Conduct a focused clinical swallowing evaluation in the acute care setting.
- Identify clinical findings associated with increased risk for oropharyngeal dysphagia.
- Interpret bedside findings within the context of respiratory, medical, and nutritional status.
- Identify the limitations of the clinical swallowing evaluation.
- Determine when instrumental swallowing assessment is indicated.
- Develop appropriate recommendations for communication, oral intake, and continued dysphagia management.
- Document clinical findings and recommendations using professional medical terminology.

## Today's Modules

### 1. Chart Review

Review Karla Green's medical history, hospital course, respiratory status, and swallowing history. Identify factors that may influence today's evaluation.

[Begin Chart Review](chart.html)

### 2. Interdisciplinary Notes

Review documentation from Respiratory Therapy, Nursing, the medical team, and other disciplines to identify information relevant to PMV candidacy and swallowing safety.

[Review Interdisciplinary Notes](interdisciplinary.html)

### 3. PMV & Swallowing Considerations

Integrate information from the chart and interdisciplinary team to plan your evaluation and determine how PMV status may influence the swallowing assessment.

[Review Evaluation Considerations](considerations.html)

### 4. Clinical Evaluation

Complete the PMV and clinical swallowing evaluation with your patient. Use information from the live patient encounter and available clinical findings to guide your assessment.

[Begin Clinical Evaluation](evaluation.html)

### 5. Clinical Findings

Review and integrate findings from today's PMV and swallowing evaluation.

[Review Clinical Findings](findings.html)

### 6. Clinical Decision & Recommendations

Determine appropriate recommendations regarding PMV use, oral intake, instrumental swallowing assessment, and continued SLP intervention.

[Complete the Simulation](clinical-decision.html)

### 7. Clinical Implications

Reflect on the strengths and limitations of the clinical swallowing evaluation and consider how today's findings influence the next steps in Karla's care.

[Clinical Implications](implications.html)
